questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Define the Cartesian plane and explain the role of the two perpendicular axes in forming this system.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Defines the Cartesian plane as a 2-D coordinate system.
Explains that it uses two perpendicular lines (axes) to mark points in 2-D space.

questions.explanationAnswer: The Cartesian plane is a two-dimensional coordinate system defined by two perpendicular lines, known as the x-axis (horizontal) and the y-axis (vertical). These axes intersect at a point called the origin, providing a structured framework to describe the exact location of any point in a 2-D space using numerical coordinates.
questions.explanationQuestion: This question tests the student's understanding of the fundamental definition of the 2-D Cartesian coordinate system as presented on page 3.
questions.correctAnswer: The Cartesian plane is a 2-D system using two perpendicular axes (x-axis and y-axis) to define locations.

questions.topic: Page 3: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 3-4 Focus)
questions.questionText: Given a point $P(x, y)$, explain what the values $x$ and $y$ represent in terms of distances from the axes.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: States that x represents the perpendicular distance from the y-axis.
States that y represents the perpendicular distance from the x-axis.

questions.explanationAnswer: For a point $P(x, y)$, the value $x$ (the x-coordinate) represents the perpendicular distance of the point from the y-axis, and the value $y$ (the y-coordinate) represents the perpendicular distance of the point from the x-axis.
questions.explanationQuestion: This question requires interpreting the meaning of coordinates as defined on page 4.
questions.correctAnswer: x is the distance from the y-axis, and y is the distance from the x-axis.
